backlog :44, no new diagnostic in the file: `grep -E "ObjectAssetCatalogue\.cs\([0-9]+,[0-9]+\): warning CS[0-9]+" <POST log> | grep -vc "warning CS1574"` prints 0. Must-fire: over the BASE log it prints at least 1 (the CS1591 lines). CS1574 is excluded here because criterion 23 owns it: the base doc build reports `ObjectAssetCatalogue.cs(7,28): warning CS1574` for the `ObjectPaletteView` cref at :7, which Gate 2 (D1) folded into this task.

backlog :44, the new `Paths` summary carries no cref, so that criterion 23 alone accounts for CS1574 in this file and no new cref is added that criterion 3's exclusion would hide: `python -I -c "import sys;L=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read().split(b'\r\n')[:-1];s=[int(x) if x else None for x in sys.argv[2].split(':')];[print(repr(l)) for l in L[slice(*s)]]" C:/dm-wt/20261109-2239-app-comment-fixes/src/DungeonMaster.App/Assets/ObjectAssets/ObjectAssetCatalogue.cs 13:-5 | grep -c cref` prints 0. This is a constraint on the new lines: at 3b6e7ef the slice is empty, so it is met there trivially and bites only once the summary exists.

backlog :44, unchanged lines preserved (mechanical, preserved behaviour): P-SLICE over C:/dm-wt/20261109-2239-app-comment-fixes/src/DungeonMaster.App/Assets/ObjectAssets/ObjectAssetCatalogue.cs prints `d7ce214763e01404f3c733060cd57db0f48d505399b439cca3a2548614157e7e` for `:6`, `0b223c4dd082b042348f03f0ffda17935da33d6fba5d4e00f69b48e15ec4b0c8` for `7:13`, and `0a57bb322cdd4f72cc18ab1e6059ac94a91627232f87d03b62a9276e79de12fc` for `-5:` (all three are the 3b6e7ef values measured by the architect; the `-5:` slice begins with the `Paths` line). Line 7 is deliberately not constrained here: criterion 23 changes it. P-SLICE is `python -I -c "import hashlib,sys;L=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read().split(b'\r\n')[:-1];s=[int(x) if x else None for x in sys.argv[2].split(':')];print(hashlib.sha256(b'\r\n'.join(L[slice(*s)])).hexdigest())" <file> <slice>`: it splits the file's bytes on CRLF, drops the empty piece after the final CRLF, and prints the sha256 of the lines selected by a Python slice (`:6` = lines 1-6, `7:13` = lines 8-13, `-5:` = the last 5 lines), re-joined with CRLF. Because it splits on CRLF, a bare LF or a lone CR inside the slice changes the digest.

backlog :44, summary shape: P-SHOW over C:/dm-wt/20261109-2239-app-comment-fixes/src/DungeonMaster.App/Assets/ObjectAssets/ObjectAssetCatalogue.cs with slice `13:-5` (the lines inserted between base line 13, the blank line after the `_paths` initializer, and the `Paths` line) prints, in order, exactly `b'\t/// <summary>'`, one or more lines each beginning `b'\t///\t\t'`, and exactly `b'\t/// </summary>'`; the text lines follow one sentence per `///` line, each line ending in `.`, never a sentence broken across two `///` lines (dm-conventions backend/dotnet-format.md section 9, 'Line breaks occur only at sentence boundaries', and the two-tab indent after `///` from the same section). Must-fire: at 3b6e7ef this slice prints nothing. P-SHOW is `python -I -c "import sys;L=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read().split(b'\r\n')[:-1];s=[int(x) if x else None for x in sys.argv[2].split(':')];[print(repr(l)) for l in L[slice(*s)]]" <file> <slice>`: same slicing as P-SLICE, printing each selected line's Python repr, so a tab shows as `\t` and cannot be confused with spaces (lesson FORM 6: never judge tabs with `\t` in a grep pattern).
